GDWebApp.listen_tls: Start an HTTPS listener from a PEM certificate chain and an unencrypted private key, selecting HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 through ALPN. Supports TLS 1.2 and 1.3. The startup result is returned as R. opts sets client_auth to none, request, require, verify_if_given, or require_and_verify; client_ca selects the client trust bundle.
GD.net.dial_tls: Dial a verified TLS connection. Options include timeout, server_name, insecure_skip_verify, ca_file, paired cert_file/key_file for client authentication, and next_protos as an array of ALPN strings. File access is permission checked on a worker. Failed authentication never falls back to plaintext.
GDTCPConn.connection_state: Inspect published handshake_complete, server_name, negotiated_protocol, and numeric TLS version without accessing active worker state. Version is zero before negotiation; 771 and 772 denote TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
GD.data.gzip_writer: Create a GDGzipWriter over a byte Writer. Compression runs on CPU workers and preserves downstream backpressure. Levels: -2 Huffman only, -1 default, 0..9. Close finishes the gzip member but leaves the destination open; reset reuses the compressor at the same level.
GDGzipWriter.header: Configure metadata before the first write, flush, or close: name/comment are non-NUL Latin-1, extra is bytes within the 65535-byte wire width, mod_time is Unix seconds, and os is a byte defaulting to 255. Reset clears metadata.
GDGzipWriter: Incremental gzip output to files, connections, or HTTP response Writers. write returns the accepted input-byte count; flush publishes buffered output; close completes the member; reset discards state and clears errors. Operations are ordered; failures remain sticky until reset. Methods suspend only the calling routine, with explicit _async variants for signals.
GDBodySource: Public base for incrementally supplying file and HTTP response bodies. Users normally work with it as GDFileStream, GDWebWriter, or GDGzipWriter.
GDWebWriter: The byte destination passed to a GD.web.stream producer. write(data, offset=0, count=-1) sends a range and returns accepted bytes, waiting while the connection is backed up. write_text(text, offset=0, count=-1) sends a character range as UTF-8. count=-1 selects the remainder. flush waits until preceding writes are sent. Detect disconnects through flush errors and request-context cancellation.
GD.web.stream: Create a lazy response producer called once with a GDWebWriter. Write PackedByteArray chunks and return void or R when finished. length=-1 selects unknown-length framing. The producer may await and should observe request-context cancellation; HEAD and bodyless statuses do not invoke it.
GD: Entry to the standard features of a command-line program: files, data, async, time, and more.
GD.web: Entry for building websites and Web APIs, with routes, static files, gdhtml templates, sessions, CSRF, JWT, rate limiting, and input validation.
GD.database: Database entry shared by SQLite and PostgreSQL. Synchronous-looking calls suspend only their GDScript; *_async returns Signals for composition.
GD.database.sqlite: Entry for opening low-level synchronous connections to embedded SQLite databases.
GD.database.postgres: Entry for creating PostgreSQL clients and connection pools.
GD.database.redis: Entry for creating Redis clients and connection pools.
Err: A value holding the kind of failure, its description, machine-readable info, cause, and working context.
R: A result retaining a success value or partial result together with an Err.
GDWebRequest: The HTTP request received by a route handler, with strict JSON, a per-request context, and streaming of large bodies.
GDDatabaseClient: Client providing shared SQLite and PostgreSQL queries, streaming Rows, first-row lookup, and connection statistics.
GDDatabaseTx: Dedicated client holding one physical connection until the transaction ends.
GDDatabaseRows: Incremental query results. Advance with next(), decode the current row with scan() or values(), inspect err(), and release resources with close().
GDSQLiteDB: Synchronous connection to the embedded SQLite.
GDSQLiteStatement: A SQLite statement prepared once and reused.
GD.async: Entry for async work: waiting, concurrency, racing, timeouts, and cancellation. spawn starts a main-thread coroutine; CPU work belongs in each standard module's _async entry points.
GD.log: Entry for ordered I/O of one line at a time with a consistent level, time, and destination. flush waits for earlier output.
GD.net: Network entry for TCP and TLS streams, listeners, UDP packets, name resolution, and address checks. TLS verifies the certificate chain and server name by default; waiting operations suspend only their caller.
GD.http: Entry for HTTP requests plus URL, query, and media-type handling. fetch suspends only its caller; fetch_async returns a Signal for composition.
GD.file: Whole-file operations and streaming file I/O suspend only their caller. This entry also provides path operations and file-format readers; *_async returns Signals for concurrent starts.
GDFileStream: Reader, Writer, and Closer for ordered incremental access to a regular file. Separate streams proceed concurrently.
GD.collection: Reshape Arrays and Dictionaries and create heaps, queues, and caches. Awaitable operations use CPU workers or the runtime ready queue; callable work cooperates with other tasks without requiring SceneTree frames.
GD.data: Data conversion for bytes, binary codecs, hashes, key derivation, and in-memory CSV, INI, TOML, YAML, JSON, XML, and related formats. Invalid input and settings return failures.
GD.id: Entry for generating and checking UUIDs and time-ordered ULIDs.
GD.text: Entry for formatting and comparing text.
GD.html: Entry for HTML entities, tags, and templates with context-sensitive escaping for text, attributes, URLs, styles, and scripts.
GDHTMLTemplate: Immutable template parsed by GD.html.template. execute renders text, execute_bytes renders UTF-8 bytes, and the value can be shared across requests.
GD.math: Entry for standard mathematical functions, IEEE 754 special values, and bit conversions.
GD.math.bits: Integer math entry for uint64 bit counts, rotations, reversals, and operations with carry.
GD.version: Entry for parsing, comparing, and range-matching Semantic Versions.
GD.time: Entry for converting and computing Unix time, ISO 8601, and HTTP dates. parse_iso accepts RFC 3339, and add and diff clamp at the 64-bit integer ends.
GD.cli: Entry for gd's version and docs, flags, and allowed environment and system information.
GD.test: Entry for small test helpers that collect asserts.
GDWebApp: Web application that listens with routes, static files, and middleware together.
GDWebServer: Low-level server using HTTP/1.1 responses for HTTP/1 requests and independent streams for TLS-negotiated HTTP/2 requests.
GDWebMiddleware: Base of middleware that inspects and reshapes a request before the handler. To write your own, pass a function or an object with handle(req).
GDWebSessionStore: In-process store of expiring sessions keyed by cookie ID.
GDWebRouteGroup: Route group sharing a prefix and middleware.
GDAsyncContext: Context passing the first cancellation reason and deadline from parent to child.
GDJSONLReader: Reader decoding JSON Lines one line at a time as chunks arrive.
GDBinaryHeap: Heap that pops the value with the smallest rank chosen by pick first.
GDPriorityQueue: Queue that pops the smallest priority number first, and insertion order among equals.
GDLRUCache: Cache holding recently used values under a count and expiry limit, creating a value when missing.
GDMemoizedCallable: Wrapper remembering a function's arguments and results in an LRU cache.
GDCLIFlags: Parser reading typed bool flags such as true/false and 1/0, integers with 0x, 0o, and 0b prefixes, and collecting positional arguments.
GDTestCheck: Checker collecting assert counts and failures and producing the test exit code.
GDPostgresClient: Client for one PostgreSQL connection. Regular methods suspend only their caller; *_async returns Signals for concurrent composition.
GDPostgresPool: Concurrency-safe pool opening PostgreSQL connections on demand up to a maximum, with a wait queue and connection statistics.
GDRedisClient: Client for one Redis connection. Regular methods suspend only their caller; *_async returns Signals for concurrent composition.
GDRedisPool: Concurrency-safe pool distributing work across several Redis connections.
GDTCPConn: Concurrency-safe TCP or TLS byte stream with FIFO reads and writes, deadlines, Close wakeups, and addresses.
GDTCPListener: TCP listener with deadlines and Close wakeups for pending accepts.
GDUDPPacketConn: UDP endpoint preserving packet boundaries and source addresses, with deadlines and Close wakeups.
GDHTTPResponse: Response holding the received HTTP status, headers, and body, returning strict JSON as an R.
GD.http.fetch: Return response, Err. Transport failures retain a partial response; HTTP 4xx/5xx are valid responses.
GD.web.json: Return response, Err and preserve encoding failures for the caller.
GD.web.view: Return response, Err and preserve file, parsing, rendering, and cancellation failures.
GD.html.fill: Return rendered text, Err. Invalid templates do not silently become empty text.
GD.cli.run: Return exit code and captured output. A nonzero exit returns Err with info.code; timeout and cancellation also retain code and output in the value.
GD.http.decode_query: Return all values per key as Arrays and the first Err, retaining valid pairs. Non-UTF-8 or NUL-containing keys and values remain PackedByteArray.
GD.http.parse_url: Parse URL structure, retaining the original raw_query and valid entries in query. Use decode_query to inspect query errors.
GD.http.build_url: Build a URL, preferring raw_query when present. Remove raw_query after editing query to regenerate its encoded representation.
GDWebRequest.query: First value of each valid query key. Use query_all for duplicate values, or decode_query on the raw query to inspect errors.
GDSQLiteStatement.one: Return the first row and Err. An empty result returns Err.NOT_FOUND.
GDRedisClient.pipeline: Always return an Array in command order, including one-command pipelines. Failure retains known replies and marks unknown replies with Err.
GDRedisClient.transaction: Return command results and Err. WATCH abort is INTERRUPTED with info.code=tx_failed; command failures retain sibling results.
GD.data.pbkdf2_sha256: Return a 32-byte derived key and Err. Iteration counts of one or less perform one iteration.
GD.data.msgpack: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.cbor: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.tar: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.to_toml: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.to_yaml: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.to_xml: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.to_env: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.to_front_matter: Return the encoded value and Err. Inputs that cannot be represented produce an Err instead of omitted entries or an empty success value.
GD.data.env: Return an environment dictionary and Err. Invalid names and unterminated quotes return an Err.
GD.http.encode_query: Encode scalar or Array values, repeating keys in byte-sorted order. PackedByteArray preserves arbitrary bytes; spaces become +.
GDWebRequest.query_all: All values for each valid query key in arrival order. Binary keys and values remain PackedByteArray.
GDRedisClient.query: Return a command value and Err. A missing value is NOT_FOUND with info.code=nil; null elements within array replies remain null. Binary bulk values remain PackedByteArray.
GD.data.base64_decode: Decode with standard padding by default; raw=true selects unpadded input. Return partial bytes with Err. Base32 uses uppercase letters.
GD.data.base32_decode: Decode with standard padding by default; raw=true selects unpadded input. Return partial bytes with Err. Base32 uses uppercase letters.
GD.data.base64url_decode: Decode the URL-safe alphabet; raw=true is the default. Set raw=false for padded input. Identity-sensitive signature parsing applies separate canonical checks.
GD.data.uncbor: Decode CBOR and report malformed UTF-8 text as Err. Valid text containing NUL remains PackedByteArray without truncation.
GD.data.unmsgpack: Decode MessagePack without losing text bytes. Non-UTF-8 or NUL-containing text remains PackedByteArray; leading BOM is preserved.
